h1: The 8 Best Cordless Electric Kettles of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best cordless electric kettles, compared on wattage, capacity, and body material so you can match one to your kitchen.
summary: The Cuisinart Electric Kettle is the best cordless electric kettle, pairing 1500W with 1.7L in the $100 to $200 bucket. The Amazon Basics stainless kettle gives 1500W in a compact 1L for less, and the COMFEE' brings full 1.7L steel under $50. The glass Amazon Basics and Chefman cover glass fans, while the Cosori, OVENTE and Hamilton Beach round out the list.
intro: People shop for cordless kettles by looks and then find that the real differences are wattage and body material. A 1500W kettle and an 1100W kettle with the same capacity do not boil in the same time, and a glass body behaves differently from steel when a child, a cat or a busy morning comes near it. Capacity decides how often you refill, and the footprint decides whether it fits.

Eight kettles were set against the Primea framework, with wattage, capacity, body material, price and spec completeness weighing most. Prices appear as buckets. Six list 1500W or close to it, two omit wattage entirely, and the material is usually clear from the title, so those three facts sort the field quickly.

products.name: Cuisinart Electric Kettle
products.verdict: The strongest all-round balance of power and capacity here.
products.description:
The Cuisinart pairs a 1500W heating element with a 1.7L capacity, which is the combination most households actually need for tea, instant noodles and pour-over coffee. It sits in the $100 to $200 price bracket. Wattage drives boil speed, and 1.7L fills a teapot and a mug at once.

It ranks first for the all-round spec, but the same numbers appear on cheaper rivals. The COMFEE' matches it at a lower price, so the Cuisinart wins on brand and polish more than on specification.

Buy it for daily tea and coffee drinkers who want one dependable kettle. The caveats are the highest price tier here and that rivals match its power for less. Skip it if you want the same specs for under $50.
products.idealFor: Daily tea and coffee drinkers who want one dependable kettle.
products.skipIf: You want the same specs for under $50.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Stainless Steel Kettle for Tea and Coffee
products.verdict: Stainless body and 1500W at a budget price.
products.description:
This kettle has a stainless steel body, 1500W of power, and a 1L capacity, in the $25 to $50 range. It is the compact member of the group. A 1L body heats faster than a 1.7L one and takes little counter space.

It lands second because the 1500W matches the Cuisinart, but the 1L capacity is smaller and needs more refills for groups. For one or two people, that does not matter.

Buy it for singles and couples who want steel on a budget. The caveats are the 1L capacity and refills for groups. Skip it if you regularly boil water for more than two people.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples who want steel on a budget.
products.skipIf: You regularly boil water for more than two people.

products.name: COMFEE' Stainless Steel Electric Kettle
products.verdict: Full-size steel body with 1500W for under $50.
products.description:
The COMFEE' offers a stainless steel body, 1500W, and a 1.7L capacity, all in the $25 to $50 range. That is the same output and size as the Cuisinart in a cheaper bracket. Steel is durable and does not shatter if knocked.

It ranks below the Amazon Basics steel pick on price only by a narrow margin, and above the glass models on durability. It lacks the brand reputation of Cuisinart.

Buy it for families who want full capacity and steel for less. The caveats are a basic spec sheet and less brand reputation. Skip it if you want a smaller, lighter kettle.
products.idealFor: Families who want full capacity and steel for less.
products.skipIf: You want a smaller, lighter kettle.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Kettle with Glass Carafe for Tea and Coffee
products.description:
This glass carafe kettle offers 1500W and 1.7L, and it sits in the under $25 tier. Glass lets you see the water level at a glance. Seeing the water also shows scale building up, which steel hides.

It ranks fourth because it matches the COMFEE' on power and size but swaps steel for glass, which is more fragile. It costs less than any steel kettle here, though.

Buy it for budget shoppers who want glass and full capacity. The caveats are that glass is more fragile and less rugged than steel. Skip it if you are rough on kitchenware or have kids around.
products.idealFor: Budget shoppers who want glass and full capacity.
products.skipIf: You are rough on kitchenware or have kids around.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle
products.verdict: The biggest capacity in the guide at 1.8L.
products.description:
Chefman gives you a glass body, 1500W, and 1.8L, the largest capacity listed in this ranking, in the under $25 tier. A bigger tank reduces refills for a family, but it needs more space and takes a little longer to come to the boil. Shared kitchens benefit most.

It ranks below the Amazon Basics glass kettle only by a narrow margin: 0.1L more capacity is a small gain, and the footprint grows. The materials and power are identical, so the choice is about capacity. If the extra 0.1L matters, take it.

Buy it for households that boil for several people at once. The caveats are a bigger counter footprint and glass that needs care. Skip it if counter space is tight.
products.idealFor: Households that boil for several people at once.

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A plastic 1.7L kettle with no wattage listed.
products.description:
The Cosori is a plastic body 1.7L kettle in the $25 to $50 range. The spec sheet we have lists no wattage. Plastic is light, which suits people who find steel heavy when full, but the missing figure leaves a gap in the spec sheet.

It ranks sixth because missing wattage makes it hard to compare boil speed with the 1500W picks. Plastic is lightweight but the least premium material here, and it can retain tastes.

Buy it for buyers who want a light kettle at a modest price. The caveats are the unlisted wattage and the plastic body. Skip it if you want confirmed boil power, since the listing never states one.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a light kettle at a modest price.

products.name: OVENTE 1.7L Electric Kettle with 1100W Fast Boiling Water
products.description:
OVENTE has a stainless steel body, 1.7L, and 1100W, in the under $25 tier. Steel and size at the lowest price is the draw, and a steel body is easy to wipe clean. A lower wattage also puts less load on a shared circuit.

It ranks seventh because 1100W is 400W below the top picks, so expect slower heating for the same volume. It does win on price for a steel kettle, but the time cost is real every morning.

Buy it for cost-focused buyers who want steel and size. The caveats are the 1100W power and slower boils than 1500W kettles. Skip it if boil speed matters to you.
products.idealFor: Cost-focused buyers who want steel and size.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1.7 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A steel 1.7L kettle with no wattage listed.
products.description:
Hamilton Beach offers a stainless steel body and 1.7L capacity in the $25 to $50 tier. Wattage is not listed in the specs we have. An established brand means easier access to parts and support, and a steel body is easy to keep clean. Few kettles list their warranty clearly, so brand reputation counts.

It ranks last because it matches the COMFEE' on material and size but gives no power figure, so you cannot judge its boil speed. There is no standout feature either.

Buy it for brand-loyal buyers who want steel. The caveats are the unlisted wattage and no standout feature. Skip it if you want confirmed wattage, because the Cuisinart and COMFEE' state theirs.

whatMatters.detail: Wattage is the heating power, and higher means faster boiling. A 1500W kettle will outpace an 1100W one with the same capacity. Look for the wattage number in the title or bullets, not just a phrase like fast boil, and avoid listings that leave it out. Higher wattage also draws more current, so check your circuit.

Capacity in liters sets how much water you boil per cycle. A 1L kettle suits a mug or two, while 1.7L suits a household. Check the listed liters and compare to how many cups you pour at once, and remember a larger tank takes longer to boil. Boil only what you need to save time and power.

Stainless steel is durable, glass shows water level but can break, and plastic is light but less premium. The material affects how the kettle ages and feels. The listing usually names the material in the title, so read it before comparing prices. Steel hides scale, glass shows it, and plastic can hold taste.

Larger capacity means a bigger base, which matters on a small counter. A 1.8L kettle takes more room than a 1L one. Check the listed dimensions against your available space, including the height under a cabinet, and leave room for the lid and cord storage. Fit matters under cabinets, because steam rises.

A listing that omits wattage leaves you guessing at performance. Missing numbers make comparison harder. Prefer products that state wattage, capacity and material clearly, as the Cuisinart and Amazon Basics models do, and treat silence as a risk. Cosori and Hamilton Beach both skip the wattage figure.

faq.q: Will a cordless kettle work with any outlet?
faq.a: A 1500W kettle needs a standard household outlet. Avoid sharing the circuit with other high-draw appliances to prevent tripping a breaker, and never use a thin extension cord, which can overheat under a 1500W load.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with kettles?
faq.a: Ignoring wattage. Two kettles with the same capacity can boil at very different speeds, as the 1500W COMFEE' and 1100W OVENTE show. The gap can be a minute or more on a full tank.

faq.q: Is the Cuisinart worth it over the COMFEE'?
faq.a: On paper they match at 1500W and 1.7L. The Cuisinart costs more, so it only pays off if you prefer its brand or want its styling. Many buyers will be happy with the COMFEE'.

faq.q: How do I set up a new kettle?
faq.a: Rinse it, boil one full batch of water, and discard it before first use. This clears manufacturing residue and any plastic smell. Repeat the rinse if the water tastes odd.

faq.q: How do I descale a kettle?
faq.a: Hard water leaves limescale, so clean the kettle periodically following the maker's guidance, and rinse thoroughly afterwards. Glass models make the buildup easy to spot, while steel hides it until the kettle slows.

faq.q: Can I use a kettle without a base?
faq.a: Cordless kettles lift off the base for pouring, but they heat only while seated on it. Never heat without water inside, and unplug the base before cleaning.

finalTake: Buy the Cuisinart if you want the strongest all-round balance, or the COMFEE' for the same specs at a lower price. The Amazon Basics steel kettle suits singles and couples, and the glass models suit people who want to see the water. Skip the Cosori and Hamilton Beach unless you can confirm wattage. Choose by wattage and capacity first.
